answer: Sybil defense rests on priced identity: an agent posts a bond the protocol holds and can slash. Registration is open, but standing is not free. Each fresh identity locks its own stake, so a gale of puppets carries separate deposits and attacker cost scales with identity count, not one cheap account. Payout weight follows verified work, pinning newcomers at the nadir until they settle output. Self-dealers get clustered by shared funding and lose stakes together. Flooding pays only if captured rewards beat capital at risk, negative while each stake exceeds expected payout. A reef, not a toll.
